title: Committee of Supply ‒ Head B (Attorney-General's Chambers)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply ‒ Head B (Attorney-General's Chambers)

sections.label: Reasons for more officers
sections.summary: The passage asks why more officers are needed, where the additional headcounts were allocated, and whether the trend will continue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It would be enlightening to know why so many more officers are needed, where these additional headcounts have been allocated, and whether this trend will continue and why.

sections.label: Briefings for private sector hires
sections.summary: The passage asks whether private sector hires at AGC receive briefings to reorientate their mindsets from serving clients to serving the public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I agree that AGC can benefit from private sector talent who inject fresh perspectives and updated market knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, do such persons receive any briefings to reorientate their mindsets to function as public officers rather than private sector lawyers, from serving a client to serving the public?

sections.label: Former MP as Deputy AG
sections.summary: The passage states concern that appointing a former Member of Parliament as Deputy Attorney-General risks undermining public confidence in the AGC's fair and independent prosecutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, I am most concerned about the recent appointment of a former Member of Parliament as the Deputy Attorney-General (AG).

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is not a personal attack against the new Deputy AG nor on his legal competence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But it is my view that filling a constitutional post in an Organ of State with a party politician is not ideal as it carries a risk of undermining public confidence in the AGC's stated mission of fair and independent prosecutions and it is a risk that is best avoided.

sections.label: Recruitment from 2011 to 2015
sections.summary: The passage states that much recruitment took place from 2011 to 2015, with a 35% increase in headcount over that period.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Much of the recruitment thus took place from 2011 to 2015, with a 35% increase in headcount over that period.

sections.label: Manpower growth pace
sections.summary: The passage states that with AGC's improved manpower situation, the same pace of manpower growth is not expected to continue into the foreseeable future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: With AGC's improved manpower situation, we do not expect the same pace of manpower growth to continue into the foreseeable future.

sections.label: AGC officers and political links
sections.summary: The passage states AG and AGC officers are not politicians or party members, but says it goes too far to suggest they must have had no prior political party links.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In our system, the AG and AGC officers are not politicians and are not members of political parties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: But it is going too far to suggest that AGC officers must not have previously had any links with any political party.

sections.label: SCs in private practice
sections.summary: Of SCs appointed in the past 10 years, only 16 were in private practice as of last month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To put matters in context, of those appointed SCs in the past 10 years, as of last month, only 16 were in private practice or remained in private practice.

sections.label: Reasons for declining public sector posts
sections.summary: Some top lawyers approached for public sector positions were unwilling to give up private practice, while Mr Hri Kumar accepted despite personal and financial cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But they are also informed by a confluence of other factors, including the willingness to make sacrifices for the public good and having a heart for public service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I can tell the House that others have been approached for public sector positions, not necessarily for AGC, including some of the top six to seven, but they were not willing to give up their private practice for a number of reasons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Hri Kumar accepted his appointment as Deputy AG despite the considerable personal and financial cost to him.

sections.label: AG and Deputy AG prosecutorial discretion
sections.summary: The Constitution gives the AG and Deputy AG wide prosecutorial discretion over charging and charges, virtually unappealable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: But does she not agree that actually, under the Constitution, AG and Deputy AG have very wide prosecutorial discretion?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: They can decide whether to charge someone, what charges to prefer and their discretion is virtually unappealable.

sections.label: Outstanding litigators identified
sections.summary: There are six to seven people considered outstanding litigators.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What I can say is that there are six to seven people who are considered outstanding litigators.

sections.label: Qualified candidate's abilities unquestioned
sections.summary: It is not appropriate to go beyond that; the person is eminently qualified and his abilities are not questioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I do not think it is appropriate to go beyond that.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He is eminently qualified, there is no question of his abilities; you do not question his abilities.

sections.label: Singapore legal institutions since Independence
sections.summary: Singapore's legal institutions since Independence, including the Judiciary, AGC, Legal Service and Bar, are much better than when taken over from the British.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You can see that the legal institutions in Singapore since Independence, whether it is Judiciary, AGC, the Legal Service, the Bar − we are one of the few countries that has made these institutions much better than from when we took over from the British, compared to all the other countries that the Member referred to.
